# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, and required certificates.
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce image layers and size.
# - build-essential: C/C++ compilers and make.
# - cmake: Required by the kripke build system.
# - git: To clone the source code from the repository.
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI implementation for containerized environments.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    wget \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone, build, and install Kripke with MPI support.
# This single RUN command performs all build steps and cleans up afterwards
# to minimize the size of the final image, as multi-stage builds are disallowed.
# The source code is cloned from the 'main' branch as requested.
# The executable is copied to /usr/local/bin to be on the system PATH.
RUN git clone --depth 1 -b main https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Note on running with MPI in containers:
# To run Kripke with MPI in a containerized environment like Kubernetes,
# you will likely need to pass specific arguments to mpirun.
# Example: mpirun -np 4 --allow-run-as-root kripke --groups 16 --zones 512
# The '--allow-run-as-root' flag is often necessary when running as the root user.
# Additional flags for network interface selection may be needed depending on the K8s CNI.

# Set the default command to the kripke executable.
CMD ["kripke"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, and required certificates.
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce image layers and size.
# - build-essential: C/C++ compilers and make.
# - cmake: Required by the kripke build system.
# - git: To clone the source code from the repository.
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI implementation for containerized environments.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    wget \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone, build, and install Kripke with MPI support.
# This single RUN command performs all build steps and cleans up afterwards
# to minimize the size of the final image, as multi-stage builds are disallowed.
# FIX: The source code is cloned from the 'master' branch, as the 'main' branch does not exist.
# The executable is copied to /usr/local/bin to be on the system PATH.
RUN git clone --depth 1 -b master https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Note on running with MPI in containers:
# To run Kripke with MPI in a containerized environment like Kubernetes,
# you will likely need to pass specific arguments to mpirun.
# Example: mpirun -np 4 --allow-run-as-root kripke --groups 16 --zones 512
# The '--allow-run-as-root' flag is often necessary when running as the root user.
# Additional flags for network interface selection may be needed depending on the K8s CNI.

# Set the default command to the kripke executable.
CMD ["kripke"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, and required certificates.
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce image layers and size.
# - build-essential: C/C++ compilers and make.
# - cmake: Required by the kripke build system.
# - git: To clone the source code from the repository.
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI implementation for containerized environments.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    wget \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone, build, and install Kripke with MPI support.
# This single RUN command performs all build steps and cleans up afterwards
# to minimize the size of the final image, as multi-stage builds are disallowed.
# FIX: The source code is cloned from the 'main' branch, and submodules are
# initialized recursively with '--recursive' to include the required BLT build system.
# The executable is copied to /usr/local/bin to be on the system PATH.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recursive -b main https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Note on running with MPI in containers:
# To run Kripke with MPI in a containerized environment like Kubernetes,
# you will likely need to pass specific arguments to mpirun.
# Example: mpirun -np 4 --allow-run-as-root kripke --groups 16 --zones 512
# The '--allow-run-as-root' flag is often necessary when running as the root user.
# Additional flags for network interface selection may be needed depending on the K8s CNI.

# Set the default command to the kripke executable.
CMD ["kripke"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, and required certificates.
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce image layers and size.
# - build-essential: C/C++ compilers and make.
# - cmake: Required by the kripke build system.
# - git: To clone the source code from the repository.
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI implementation for containerized environments.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    wget \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone, build, and install Kripke with MPI support.
# This single RUN command performs all build steps and cleans up afterwards
# to minimize the size of the final image, as multi-stage builds are disallowed.
# FIX: The source code is cloned from the 'develop' branch, as 'main' does not exist.
# Submodules are initialized recursively with '--recursive' to include the required BLT build system.
# The executable is copied to /usr/local/bin to be on the system PATH.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recursive -b develop https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Note on running with MPI in containers:
# To run Kripke with MPI in a containerized environment like Kubernetes,
# you will likely need to pass specific arguments to mpirun.
# Example: mpirun -np 4 --allow-run-as-root kripke --groups 16 --zones 512
# The '--allow-run-as-root' flag is often necessary when running as the root user.
# Additional flags for network interface selection may be needed depending on the K8s CNI.

# Set the default command to the kripke executable.
CMD ["kripke"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, and required certificates.
# FIX: A newer version of CMake is required. The official Kitware APT repository
# is added to provide a version of CMake that meets the build requirements (>3.23).
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list >/dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone, build, and install Kripke with MPI support.
# This single RUN command performs all build steps and cleans up afterwards
# to minimize the size of the final image, as multi-stage builds are disallowed.
# FIX: The source code is cloned from the 'main' branch as originally requested.
# Submodules are initialized recursively with '--recursive' to include the required BLT build system.
# The executable is copied to /usr/local/bin to be on the system PATH.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recursive -b main https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Note on running with MPI in containers:
# To run Kripke with MPI in a containerized environment like Kubernetes,
# you will likely need to pass specific arguments to mpirun.
# Example: mpirun -np 4 --allow-run-as-root kripke --groups 16 --zones 512
# The '--allow-run-as-root' flag is often necessary when running as the root user.
# Additional flags for network interface selection may be needed depending on the K8s CNI.

# Set the default command to the kripke executable.
CMD ["kripke"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, and required certificates.
# A newer version of CMake is required, so we add the Kitware APT repository.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list >/dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone, build, and install Kripke with MPI support.
# This single RUN command performs all build steps and cleans up afterwards
# to minimize the size of the final image, as multi-stage builds are disallowed.
# FIX: The source code is cloned from the 'main' branch, as requested.
# FIX: The build system produces 'kripke.exe', which is now correctly copied to /usr/local/bin/kripke.
# Submodules are initialized recursively with '--recursive' to include the required BLT build system.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recursive -b main https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Note on running with MPI in containers:
# To run Kripke with MPI in a containerized environment like Kubernetes,
# you will likely need to pass specific arguments to mpirun.
# Example: mpirun -np 4 --allow-run-as-root kripke --groups 16 --zones 512
# The '--allow-run-as-root' flag is often necessary when running as the root user.
# Additional flags for network interface selection may be needed depending on the K8s CNI.

# Set the default command to the kripke executable.
CMD ["kripke"]

FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, and required certificates.
# A newer version of CMake is required, so we add the Kitware APT repository.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list >/dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone, build, and install Kripke with MPI support.
# This single RUN command performs all build steps and cleans up afterwards
# to minimize the size of the final image, as multi-stage builds are disallowed.
# FIX: The source code is cloned from the 'master' branch, as the requested 'main' branch does not exist.
# The build system produces 'kripke.exe', which is correctly copied to /usr/local/bin/kripke.
# Submodules are initialized recursively with '--recursive' to include the required BLT build system.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recursive -b master https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Note on running with MPI in containers:
# To run Kripke with MPI in a containerized environment like Kubernetes,
# you will likely need to pass specific arguments to mpirun.
# Example: mpirun -np 4 --allow-run-as-root kripke --groups 16 --zones 512
# The '--allow-run-as-root' flag is often necessary when running as the root user.
# Additional flags for network interface selection may be needed depending on the K8s CNI.

# Set the default command to the kripke executable.
CMD ["kripke"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Kripke benchmark
# within the Flux Framework on a single Kubernetes node.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # Deploys to the default namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to deploy, set to 1 to run on a single node
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) to run for the job
  tasks: 4

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux operator
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD
    strict: true

  # Ensure the job resources are not cleaned up after completion for inspection
  cleanup: false

  # The main container specification for the application
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to be executed by flux. The Flux Operator prepends 'flux run -n <tasks>'
      command: kripke
      # The main application container is not the launcher pod
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest runs the Kripke benchmark on a specific
# high-performance ARM-based AWS instance, resolving the previous MPI rank error.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # Deploys to the default namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The job will run on one node, as required.
  size: 1
  # Increased tasks to 64 to fully utilize the vCPUs of the selected hpc7g.16xlarge instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Defines pod-specific settings, including scheduling constraints.
  pod:
    # Selects a specific AWS instance type for this job, targeting a 64-core ARM machine.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Flux-specific configuration required for the targeted architecture.
  flux:
    # Specifies the target architecture is ARM.
    arch: "arm"
    # Overrides the default Flux view container to use an ARM-compatible image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Ensures the job resources are not cleaned up after completion for inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Defines the application container to be run under Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command is updated with a decomposition (--procs 4,4,4) that matches the 64 tasks,
      # correcting the 'Number of MPI ranks must match decomposition' error.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4
      # This is the application container, not the launcher.
      launcher: false

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest resolves the Kripke assertion failure by
# adjusting the problem domain size to be compatible with the process decomposition.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The job will run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks matches the vCPUs of the c7a.12xlarge instance.
  tasks: 48

  # Pod specification to schedule the job on a specific AWS instance type.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Flux-specific configuration. Empty as the target is a standard x86_64 architecture.
  flux: {}

  # Ensure the job resources are not cleaned up after completion for inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Define the application container to be run under Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # This is the application container, not the launcher.
      launcher: false
      # The command is corrected to fix the 'Number of zones... must evenly divide' error.
      # By setting Z-dimension zones to 15 (--zones 16,16,15), it becomes evenly divisible
      # by the 3 processes requested for that dimension (--procs 4,4,3).
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,3 --zones 16,16,15

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

Decision 4: STOP

Agent's Rationale: The previous attempt on the c6a.16xlarge (AMD) instance yielded a significant performance increase, more than doubling the figure of merit from the next best run. This indicates a strong synergy between the application and this specific CPU architecture and core count. Further architectural exploration is unlikely to yield better results, and this configuration represents a well-optimized state.
